what: C2 of the ETH model-gap lane: claimbox's proof that Anthropic's ETHIsFalse implies complexitylib's ¬ETH on cslib's multitape Turing machine, decided here from claimbox's pinned commit with our own statement pin, axioms files, nanoda (with two negative controls) and leanchecker --fresh, and three planted wrong variants that must be refused.

claim.authors: the statement by hand (cert-machine's operator session); the proof by an AI agent (Claude), in claimbox

scope: If Anthropic's ETHIsFalse holds (for every δ > 0 a deterministic Mathlib FinTM2 machine decides 3-SAT on duplicate-free formulas written as encClauses 3 within ⌊c·2^(δ·n)⌋ steps), then complexitylib's ETH is false: for every δ > 0 a deterministic cslib multitape Turing machine decides 3-SAT on every formula, written as the binary encCNF, within c·2^(δ·n)·(L+1)^e + c steps. Decided: the statement byte-equal to the pin, MainResults.lean byte-equal to Anthropic's, the three standard axioms, nanoda accepting all 23,430 declarations beneath it, leanchecker --fresh, and the three planted variants refused.
reading: MainResults.lean is Anthropic's file byte for byte, but elaborated here against complexitylib's Mathlib (Lean v4.36.0-rc2), not Anthropic's (v4.33.1). That ETHIsFalse here means what Anthropic proved there is the version seam: read, not decided.

C2 is an implication. Its conclusion is already proved outright by complexitylib's own not_eth (certs/eth-cslib-d1.json); what C2 adds is the link from a lab's statement to the standard machine, so Anthropic's proof, and with Hawkley's chain OpenAI's, refutes ETH on cslib's multitape machine with encCNF, up to the seam.
claimbox and cert-machine have the same operator: this decision separates the roles of author and checker; it is not a second party.
